To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
public consultation processes in the nuclear waste policy process are constrained and constrained in ways that affect the outcomes of consultation processes.

1) the objectives of consultation can clash with the other objectives of the policy process; 2) this is because the norms under which the consultation is conducted clash with other institutionalized policy process norms; and 3) the design of the consultation process can be constrained by these other policy process norms, which can result in a process design that does not meet the objectives of consultation.
public consultation can clash in practice with other policy objectives and that this phenomenon is evident in our case study.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the institutional norms that underpin the policy process, and how these norms shape policy outcomes.
the institutional design of public policy processes and how the design of such processes shapes outcomes.
the design of policy processes that will enable governments to reconcile potentially competing policy process objectives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
consultation is not the solution to all policy process problems.
public participation is a valuable tool, but it must be used in a manner which is consistent with the norms of the wider policy process.
the process of public consultation for the selection of a nuclear waste facility in Australia has not been successful.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we need to understand the institutional norms and values which underpin public participation and the policy process more generally.

the case shows that consultation processes are constrained by a range or range of policy process institutional norms, including those that are associated with representative democracy, the separation of powers and the rule of law, and the need to maintain the legitimacy of government decision-making.
the process of selecting a site to dispose of nuclear waste has been characterised by an absence of consultation.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the design of consultation processes needs to be carefully considered to ensure that the process is not only legitimate but also effective in delivering outcomes that meet the objectives of the policy process.
public participation is a necessary but insufficient condition for the legitimacy of public policy.
consultation can be a useful tool for policy makers to use to build support for their policy decisions.
